alignments.note: Negator realized by *no*. ἄλλα is not a negative indefinite, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty οὐ, and rule 87's joining does not apply either: the ASV writes *no* and *other* as separate words each answering to a source token, which is rule 39's test for the ordinary split.
Substantival adjective expanded with the generic noun *things*; rule 17's generic-noun clause keeps the head on the adjective, as `all things` heads on *All*.
Inflected verb takes its English subject; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition riding along under rule 21; no article stands to carry it.

ἀλλ᾽ ἤ is rendered by the single word *than*, which is the ordinary gloss of ἤ; rule 39's noncompositional cluster is scoped to a particle fused with μή, so ἤ takes the word and ἀλλά realizes nothing. Joining the pair into one aligned unit headed on ἀλλά remains defensible.
Comparative particle taking *than*; see the note on ἀλλά for the competing single-unit reading.
Relative pronoun rendered by a bare *what* with no supplied nominal, so rule 77's generic-noun arm does not arise.
Verb with its supplied subject pronoun; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.
Intensifying καί realized by *even*; rule 65 decides it on the English alone and here the ASV writes a word for it.
Second-person verb sharing the subject *ye* the ASV already wrote for ἀναγινώσκετε; that token is spent there and the verb stands alone.
Verb with its supplied subject pronoun; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.

English drops the complementizer after *hope*. Rule 43's test is the presence of an English word, not whether the clause is reported, and no word answers to ὅτι. A reference comparison reporting this is not a correction.
Improper preposition rendered by a single English preposition, so rule 42's supplied-frame question and rule 71's head question do not arise.
The Greek is anarthrous, so under rule 51 the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the word it determines; rule 42's *unto the* case needs an article to ride with and there is none here.
Future verb with its supplied subject and auxiliary; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb rather than on *will*.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged. Partition verified: s001-s018 and t001-t024 each appear exactly once, every aligned unit has nonempty arrays on both sides, and every head is a member of its own array.

ἀλλ᾽ ἤ → *than* is the one genuinely open unit. The single English word is ἤ's own ordinary gloss, so ἀλλά is left unrepresented rather than joined; but a single aligned unit over both particles headed on ἀλλά is defensible under rule 39's test read the other way. Both members recorded medium.

οὐ → *no* is kept separate from ἄλλα → *other things*. Rule 87 joins a negator to a quantifier only where the ASV writes the negation once as a single word; here it writes *no* and *other* separately, each answering to a token, so rule 2 splits them. Rules 41 and 59 are not in play at all, ἄλλα being no kind of negative.

ὅτι after ἐλπίζω is unrepresented under rule 43's English-side test, the ASV writing no complementizer. Rule 85 does not bear on it: no non-finite complement is expanded here, the ὅτι clause already being finite in Greek.

ἕως τέλους: no Greek article stands here, so the supplied *the* is a rule 51 helper on τέλους rather than anything ἕως carries; rule 42's *unto the* case needs an article to ride with. ἕως is rendered by one English word, so rule 71's improper-preposition frame head is not engaged.
t011 *ye* is spent on ἀναγινώσκετε, which is why ἐπιγινώσκετε (s012) is a bare *acknowledge* while the later ἐπιγνώσεσθε (s018) keeps its own supplied *ye will*.
